small_guidance:
- The fused bias+tanh epilogue is already cheap; the conv_transpose dominates the 17.1ms runtime. Minor tuning (BLOCK_SIZE 4096 vs 8192, num_warps 8) on the epilogue will not move the needle. Confirm cudnn is actually picking a channels_last-friendly algo by also setting `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True` before first call (already done) and warming up.
- Try folding the bias subtraction into a precomputed conv bias: `effective_bias = conv_transpose.bias - self.bias.view(-1)` at forward time, then only apply tanh in the Triton kernel. This removes one parameter load per element.
- If keeping the current structure, autotune the epilogue over {BLOCK_SIZE: 2048,4096,8192,16384} × {num_warps: 4,8} — but expected gain is <2%.
large_guidance:
- The torch ConvTranspose2d is the bottleneck (output is 32×64×512×512 ≈ 537M elements, kernel 4×4 stride 2). Replace it with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, input-spatial tile, IC tile) computing the outer product `input[n,ic,h,w] * weight[ic,oc,kh,kw]` and scatter-adding into the output grid at `(2h+kh-1, 2w+kw-1)`. Fuse conv_bias − self.bias and tanh into the final epilogue after all contributions are accumulated (two-pass: accumulate then activate, or use atomics + a separate activation pass that reads/writes once).
- Alternative: gather-style direct kernel — one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile) where each output pixel iterates over the (kh,kw,ic) taps that land on it (only positions where (oh+pad-kh) % stride == 0). This avoids atomics. With stride=2, kernel=4, each output pixel sees exactly 4 taps per ic — very compact inner loop. Use channels_last layout so IC reduction is contiguous.
- Fold both biases into the kernel epilogue: `acc = acc + conv_bias[oc] - self.bias[oc]; out = tanh(acc)` before store. This eliminates the separate epilogue kernel entirely and saves one full read/write of the 537M-element tensor (~4GB of traffic).
